title: Characterizing states outside the stop set
statement: For a set $E\subseteq\mathrm{Option}(S)$, element $a\in S$, and $q\in\mathrm{Option}(S)$, $q$ lies outside the set consisting of the absent state, $a$ as a present state, and all elements of $E$ if and only if there is some $s\in S$ such that $q$ is the present state $s$, $s\ne a$, and the present state $s$ does not belong to $E$.
hypotheses_covered: $E$ is a set of optional elements of $S$
